about:
Stixon Labels operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it was established in 1991 by founder Robert W. Chavez. The business traces its roots to 1955 when Chavez began designing and selling labels, adding flexible packaging in 1961 and forming New Mexico Plastics in 1985. Today the company is owned by Chavez’s daughters—Beverly, Julie, Barbara, and Cristina—who grew up in the label manufacturing business and now lead it as a family-owned operation.

The company manufactures custom pressure-sensitive labels and flexible packaging using flexographic printing, producing labels up to 13.75 by 15 inches. It also provides design and artwork services through a computerized art department, foil stamping, and thermal-transfer blank labels. The staff includes press operators with tenures exceeding 30 years, and most employees have been with the company for more than 15 years.

Stixon serves wineries, distilleries, food and beverage producers, and personal-care brands. Its client list includes Gruet Winery and St. Clair Winery in New Mexico, Headframe Spirits in Montana, Dion’s Pizza Salad Dressings, 505 Southwestern Chile & Salsa, El Pinto Chile & Salsa, New Mexico Piñon Coffee, Sombra Professional Therapy Products, and Marble Brewery, along with retail packaging such as foil-stamped shopping bags.

The company emphasizes service as its differentiator, offering creative, cost-effective solutions from design to finished product. Its long-tenured team and family ownership are cited as reasons for consistent quality and responsiveness.
